data_section_full_text:
4. Sample construction, sample composition, and descriptive statistics

Sample construction


Our primary sample consists of 16,310 firm-year observations for 3,262 unique firms during the pre-IFRS period (2002–2004) and post-IFRS period (2006–2007). <sup>14</sup> This includes a
treatment sample of 1,631 first-time IFRS adopters from 20 countries requiring IFRS
beginning in 2005, and 1,631 benchmark firms from 15 countries not requiring IFRS
adoption. We include firms with COMPUSTAT Global Currency data available from
2000 through 2007, when necessary, to adjust for changes in reporting currency. <sup>15</sup> We

14. We omit 2005 (the adoption year) from our sample and all tests. The tenor of our results is unchanged if
we include 2005, however.
15. For example, we calculate change variables when estimating accruals. When firms change reporting currencies (generally a switch from domestic currencies to the Euro) we translate the beginning currency (t     - 1)
into the ending currency (t) using the COMPUSTAT conversion rate as of t    - 1.

retain firms that have the necessary COMPUSTAT Global Industrial/Commercial data
and COMPUSTAT Global Issue data available for 2002 through 2007 for our tests of
income smoothing (the least restrictive specification).For each test we use a balanced sample where each treatment firm, and its matched benchmark firm, has three (two) full years
of data in the pre-adoption (post-adoption) periods. We restrict the pre-adoption period
to the three years prior to the IFRS adoption year to reduce the likelihood of other factors confounding our results. Table 1 describes the sample selection process for IFRS
adopters in detail for all remaining specifications.

We identify mandatory IFRS adopters using COMPUSTAT Global Industrial, which
identifies the set of accounting standards a firm uses to prepare its financial statements.
We code a firm-year observation as complying with IFRS if COMPUSTAT reports the
variable ASTD as “DI” based on references to IFRS in the firms’ financial statements. <sup>16</sup>

Once a firm first reports IFRS as its accounting standard in 2005, we code all subsequent
years as IFRS.
